about: SCOOT is ISCA's guide to online training resources in Speech Communication, created and long maintained by members of the ISCA community (the archived pages credit course material by Roger Moore, Simon King and many others). Its motto: 'SCOOT will never be finished.'

SCOOT 2.0 preserves the original topic structure and all 104 resource entries from the 31 August 2026 snapshot, alongside 118 clearly marked extensions. Original entries retain their descriptions and source links. Archived copies are provided where available for links reported as unavailable.

It serves the same audience as the original: students of speech communication arriving from phonetics, linguistics, computer science, or electrical engineering, anywhere between a first degree and a PhD.

The ISCA SIG directory, seminars, events and recordings moved to the independent ISCA SIG Atlas on 3 October 2026. Use the direct link at the top of this page. The Spoken LLM Benchmark Atlas also has its own dedicated page.

This is NOT an official ISCA publication. The project began as Hung-yi Lee prompting an AI agent to explore what AI agents can do. This rebuilt catalog has not been independently verified by a human, and listing a resource does not imply endorsement.
how_it_works: Original entries (marked ⬤ Original SCOOT) are faithful transcriptions of the original pages — same resources, same descriptions lightly edited for typos. The HTML snapshots they were transcribed from are preserved with the project source materials and audited mechanically against this page.

Extension entries are marked “SCOOT 2.0 extensions”. Link-status labels reflect the last recorded audit, whose timestamp is shown below; this interface update is not a new review of every resource. Catalog and link checks are not currently scheduled. Check linked course pages for current availability, pricing and versions.
Every editorial change is recorded in the changelog below, including changes made in response to community suggestions.
contribute: Found a broken link, missing resource or unclear description? Send the resource URL, its topic, and the correction you suggest.

Two ways to reach the curator: email (button below), or open an issue on the GitHub repository at github.com/speechlab0210/scoot — the catalog data lives there as plain JSON, so you can point at the exact entry.

This prototype is assembled by an AI agent. Suggestions are treated as information about the catalog, not instructions to perform unrelated actions. Contacting the curator does not guarantee an immediate reply or update.
